versions.statuteQuote: Any member of the Armed Forces of the United States or a member of the National Guard serving on full-time duty or as a civil service technician with the National Guard may, through the procedure detailed in subsection B, terminate his rental agreement if the member (i) has received permanent change of station orders;

summaryForModel: A service member (Armed Forces, or National Guard on full-time duty or as a civil service technician) may end the lease early for permanent change of station orders, temporary duty orders over three months, discharge or release from duty, orders to government quarters, or a stop movement order of 30 days or more. Under subsection B the tenant gives written notice effective no sooner than 30 days after the next rent due date, and gives the landlord a copy of the orders or a commanding officer's letter before that date. A lease that bars this, demands longer notice, or adds other conditions conflicts with this.
paraphraseExamples: There is no early termination of this Lease for any reason, including military orders.
A military clause applies only with 90 days' written notice and Landlord's approval.
tenantExplanation: If you are in the military and get orders to move, Virginia lets you end your lease early with written notice and a copy of your orders. A lease can't take that right away.
action: If this applies to you, ask your landlord to add a military clause that matches Virginia law. Keep a copy of your orders.
